Query BigQuery as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__bigquery.R
oauth_db_bigquery_api.Rd

Run GoogleSQL and browse datasets with the visitor's Google account. Queries return data frames for use in your Shiny app.

Usage

oauth_db_bigquery_api(
  authorization,
  project,
  dataset = NULL,
  location = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 300,
  page_size = 10000L,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

project

Google Cloud project in which to run and bill queries.

dataset

Default dataset for unqualified table names, or NULL.

location

Dataset location, such as "EU" or "us-central1". NULL lets BigQuery choose it.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds to submit, poll, and fetch an operation.

page_size

Maximum number of rows requested per result page.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

An R6 client with these methods:

  • $query(sql, parameters = NULL, parameter_types = NULL, maximum_bytes_billed = NULL, use_query_cache = TRUE, raw = FALSE) runs GoogleSQL and returns a data frame.

  • $datasets() lists dataset IDs in the project.

  • $tables(dataset) lists table IDs. If omitted, dataset uses the client's default.

Details

Create the client inside server() and call its methods inside render or reactive expressions. Use oauth_db_bigquery_client() for Google sign-in. Users need permission to create query jobs in project and read the data. The client uses BigQuery's REST API; bigrquery and ODBC aren't required.

Query parameters

Supply named R values in parameters, such as list(country = "NL") for SQL containing @country. Supported values include character, logical, integer, numeric, Date, and POSIXct.

Vectors become ARRAY parameters. Use a named character vector of parameter_types to override the scalar element type or type a NULL value. Use "ARRAY<INT64>" for a one-element array.

Query options

Set maximum_bytes_billed to limit the bytes a query may bill. Set use_query_cache = FALSE to disable cached query results.

Result types

INT64 and decimal columns remain strings to preserve precision. DATE becomes Date, TIMESTAMP becomes UTC POSIXct, and nested or repeated fields become list columns. BYTES fields keep their REST representation.

raw = TRUE returns an R list with the combined REST response, schema, and job reference. DML may return a data frame with no columns; use the raw result to inspect numDmlAffectedRows.

Longer queries

Queries run synchronously and collect their results in R memory. A timeout or sign-out stops fetching results but doesn't cancel a submitted BigQuery job.

Each request obtains a current token for the authorization that started the operation. A 401 response triggers one refresh attempt. Other errors stop the operation without resubmitting SQL.

See also

oauth_db_bigquery_client(). vignette("bigquery", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Other platform API clients: oauth_db_clickhouse_api(), oauth_db_cratedb_api(), oauth_db_databricks_api(), oauth_db_fabric_api(), oauth_db_libsql_api(), oauth_db_opensearch_api(), oauth_db_postgrest_api()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
bigquery <- oauth_db_bigquery_api(
  auth$connection, project = "billing-project", location = "EU"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  bigquery$query(
    "SELECT * FROM reporting.Orders WHERE country = @country LIMIT 20",
    parameters = list(country = "NL")
  )
})
} # }
